question: what is science
what do scientists do
what is the scientific method
answer: Science is how we find out about the world by asking questions, testing ideas with experiments, and looking at the evidence. Scientists ask, guess (hypothesis), test, record results and share what they learn.

question: what is a hypothesis
what is an experiment
what is a fair test
answer: A hypothesis is a smart guess you can test. An experiment tests it. In a fair test, you change only one thing at a time and keep everything else the same.

question: what do plants need to grow
what do plants need
what do plants need to survive
answer: Plants need sunlight, water, air (carbon dioxide) and nutrients from the soil to grow.

question: what is photosynthesis
how do plants make food
how do plants make their food
answer: Photosynthesis is how green plants make their food. Leaves use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar for energy, and they give out oxygen for us to breathe.

question: what is chlorophyll
why are leaves green
answer: Chlorophyll is the green substance in leaves that traps sunlight so plants can make food. It's why leaves are green!

question: what are the parts of a plant
what does a root do
what does a stem do
what do roots do
answer: Roots hold the plant in the soil and take in water. The stem carries water and food and holds the plant up. Leaves make food. Flowers make seeds so new plants can grow.

question: how does a seed grow
what is germination
how do seeds grow into plants
answer: A seed germinates when it gets water, air and warmth. It swells and splits, a tiny root grows down, and a shoot grows up toward the light.

question: what is pollination
what do bees do for flowers
why are bees important
answer: Pollination is when pollen moves from one flower to another so that seeds and fruits can form. Bees, butterflies and other insects carry pollen as they visit flowers, and that's why bees are so important for our food!

question: what is a cell
what are cells
what is the basic unit of life
answer: A cell is the smallest living building block of all plants and animals. Your body is made of trillions of cells!

question: what is the difference between plant and animal cells
what is a nucleus
what is a cell wall
answer: Both have a nucleus, the control centre of the cell. Plant cells also have a stiff cell wall and green chloroplasts for making food, which animal cells don't have.

question: what are the states of matter
what are the three states of matter
what is matter
what is a solid liquid and gas
answer: Matter is anything that takes up space and has mass. It comes in three main states: solid (keeps its shape), liquid (flows and takes the shape of its container) and gas (spreads out to fill any space).

question: what is melting
what is freezing
what is evaporation
what is condensation
answer: Melting turns a solid into a liquid. Freezing turns a liquid into a solid. Evaporation turns a liquid into a gas. Condensation turns a gas into a liquid.

question: at what temperature does water boil
what is the boiling point of water
when does water boil
answer: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.

question: at what temperature does water freeze
what is the freezing point of water
when does water freeze
answer: Water freezes into ice at 0 degrees Celsius.

question: what is the water cycle
how does the water cycle work
how does rain form
where does rain come from
answer: In the water cycle, the sun heats water so it evaporates into vapour. The vapour rises, cools and condenses into clouds, then falls as rain, called precipitation. The water flows back to rivers and seas, and it starts all over again!

question: what is the solar system
tell me about the solar system
what is in the solar system
answer: The solar system is the Sun and everything that travels around it: eight planets, their moons, asteroids and comets.

question: how many planets are there
how many planets are in the solar system
what are the planets
name the planets
answer: There are eight planets. In order from the Sun they are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

question: what is the biggest planet
which is the largest planet
what is the largest planet in the solar system
answer: Jupiter is the biggest planet. More than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it!

question: what is the smallest planet
which is the smallest planet
answer: Mercury is the smallest planet, and it's also the closest to the Sun.

question: which planet is the hottest
what is the hottest planet
answer: Venus is the hottest planet, because its thick clouds trap heat, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

question: which planet is called the red planet
what is the red planet
why is mars red
answer: Mars is called the Red Planet because its soil is rusty iron oxide, which is red.

question: which planet has rings
what planet has the most beautiful rings
tell me about saturn
answer: Saturn is famous for its beautiful rings of ice and rock. Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune have rings too, but they're much fainter.

question: what is the sun
what is the sun made of
is the sun a star
answer: The Sun is a star, a giant ball of hot glowing gas, mostly hydrogen and helium. It gives us light and heat, and our whole solar system moves around it.

question: what is the moon
why does the moon change shape
what are the phases of the moon
how long does the moon take to go around the earth
answer: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite. It doesn't make its own light but reflects sunlight. As it orbits Earth, we see different amounts of its lit side, which are the phases. One orbit takes about 27 days.

question: what is an eclipse
what is a solar eclipse
what is a lunar eclipse
answer: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon moves between the Earth and the Sun and blocks the sunlight. A lunar eclipse happens when Earth's shadow falls on the Moon. Never look straight at the Sun!

question: why do we have day and night
what causes day and night
how does the earth rotate
answer: The Earth spins like a top, once every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day, and the side facing away has night.

question: why do we have seasons
what causes the seasons
how long does the earth take to go around the sun
answer: Earth travels around the Sun once every year (365 days). Because Earth is tilted, different parts get more or less sunlight at different times, which makes the seasons. Near the equator, like Ghana, we have a wet and a dry season.

question: what is gravity
why do things fall down
why do things fall
what is the force of gravity
answer: Gravity is the invisible force that pulls things toward each other. Earth's gravity pulls everything toward its centre, which is why things fall down and why we stay on the ground. Isaac Newton explained it!

question: what is a force
what are forces
what is friction
what are push and pull
answer: A force is a push or a pull. Forces can make things start moving, stop, speed up, slow down or change shape. Friction is a force that slows things down when they rub together.

question: what is energy
what are the forms of energy
what types of energy are there
answer: Energy is the ability to do work or make things happen. It comes in many forms: light, heat, sound, electrical, chemical (like food), kinetic (movement) and potential (stored).

question: what is renewable energy
what are the sources of renewable energy
what is solar energy
what is clean energy
answer: Renewable energy comes from sources that don't run out, like sunlight (solar), wind, flowing water (hydro) and heat from the Earth. It's clean because it doesn't make much pollution. Ghana has lots of sunshine and the Akosombo hydroelectric dam!

question: what are fossil fuels
what is coal oil and gas
why are fossil fuels bad
answer: Fossil fuels, like coal, oil and natural gas, formed from ancient plants and animals over millions of years. When we burn them they release carbon dioxide, which warms the planet, so we use renewable energy more and more.

question: what is electricity
how does electricity work
what is electric current
answer: Electricity is a form of energy made by the flow of tiny charged particles called electrons through a wire. We use it to power lights, phones and computers. Be careful: never touch plugs or sockets with wet hands!

question: what is a circuit
what is an electric circuit
how do i make a circuit
what do you need for a circuit
answer: A circuit is a complete loop that electricity can travel around. You need a power source like a battery, wires, and something to power like a bulb. If the loop is broken, for example by an open switch, the bulb goes off.

question: what is a conductor
what is an insulator
what materials conduct electricity
which materials are good conductors
answer: A conductor lets electricity flow through it, like copper, iron and other metals. An insulator, like plastic, rubber, wood and glass, doesn't. That's why electric wires are metal inside and plastic outside.

question: what is a magnet
how do magnets work
what do magnets attract
what is magnetism
answer: A magnet is an object that attracts things made of iron, like nails and paperclips. Every magnet has a north and a south pole. Opposite poles attract, and the same poles push each other away.

question: what is light
how does light travel
what is the speed of light
how fast is light
answer: Light is energy we can see. It travels in straight lines and is super fast, about 300,000 kilometres every second. Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth!

question: what is a rainbow
how is a rainbow made
what are the colours of the rainbow
what are the colors of the rainbow
answer: A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through raindrops and splits into colours. The seven colours are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
keywords: red orange yellow green blue indigo violet

question: what is a shadow
how are shadows made
why do we have shadows
answer: A shadow forms when an object blocks light. The light can't pass through, so a dark shape appears behind it. Shadows are longer in the morning and evening and shorter at midday.

question: what is a reflection
what is a mirror
how do mirrors work
answer: Reflection is when light bounces off a surface. A mirror is very smooth and shiny, so it reflects light neatly and gives you an image of yourself.

question: what is sound
how does sound travel
how do we hear
what makes sound
answer: Sound is made when things vibrate (shake quickly back and forth). The vibrations travel as waves through air, water or solids to our ears. Sound can't travel in space because there's no air!

question: what is an echo
how does an echo work
answer: An echo is a sound that bounces off a hard surface, like a wall or a mountain, and comes back to your ears.

question: what is pitch
what is loud and quiet sound
what is volume of sound
answer: Pitch is how high or low a sound is: fast vibrations make high sounds, slow ones make low sounds. Volume is how loud a sound is, and bigger vibrations make louder sounds.

question: what is a food chain
what is a food web
what are producers and consumers
what are producers
answer: A food chain shows who eats whom and how energy passes along. It starts with a producer, a plant that makes food from sunlight, then consumers: herbivores eat plants, and carnivores eat other animals. Decomposers break down dead things.

question: what is a herbivore
what is a carnivore
what is an omnivore
what do herbivores eat
answer: Herbivores eat only plants, like cows, goats and elephants. Carnivores eat only meat, like lions and crocodiles. Omnivores eat both plants and animals, like humans, chickens and bears.

question: what is a habitat
what is an ecosystem
what is an environment in science
answer: A habitat is the natural home of a plant or animal, where it finds food, water and shelter, like a forest, pond or savannah. An ecosystem is all the living and non-living things in a place and how they depend on each other.

question: what is a mammal
what are mammals
give me examples of mammals
answer: Mammals are warm-blooded animals that have hair or fur and feed their babies milk. Humans, dogs, elephants, bats and whales are all mammals.

question: what is a reptile
what are reptiles
what is an amphibian
what are amphibians
answer: Reptiles, like snakes, lizards and crocodiles, are cold-blooded and have dry scaly skin. Amphibians, like frogs, live part of their lives in water and part on land, and have soft moist skin.

question: what is a bird
how do birds fly
what are the features of birds
answer: Birds are warm-blooded animals with feathers, wings and beaks, and they lay eggs. Most birds can fly, but some, like ostriches and penguins, can't.

question: what is an insect
how many legs does an insect have
how many legs do insects have
answer: An insect has six legs and three body parts: head, thorax and abdomen. Most have wings and antennae. Ants, bees, butterflies and mosquitoes are insects.

question: how many legs does a spider have
is a spider an insect
how many legs do spiders have
answer: A spider has eight legs and two body parts, so it's not an insect. It's an arachnid.

question: what is a life cycle
what is the life cycle of a butterfly
what is metamorphosis
answer: A butterfly goes through four stages, called metamorphosis: egg, then caterpillar (larva), then chrysalis (pupa), then adult butterfly.

question: what is the life cycle of a frog
how does a tadpole become a frog
answer: A frog starts as an egg, hatches into a tadpole with a tail and gills, grows back legs and then front legs, loses its tail, and becomes an adult frog that breathes air.

question: how many bones are in the human body
how many bones does an adult have
how many bones do humans have
answer: An adult human has 206 bones. Babies are born with about 300 bones, and some join together as they grow.

question: what does the heart do
what is the heart
how does the heart work
what pumps blood
answer: The heart is a strong muscle that pumps blood around your body, carrying oxygen and food to every part. It beats about 100,000 times each day!

question: what do the lungs do
what are lungs
how do we breathe
how do we breathe in and out
answer: The lungs help us breathe. When you breathe in, they take in oxygen from the air. When you breathe out, they push out carbon dioxide.

question: what does the brain do
what is the brain
what controls the body
answer: The brain is the control centre of your body. It lets you think, learn, remember, feel and move, and it controls everything your body does, even while you sleep.

question: what are the five senses
what are the senses
how many senses do we have
answer: We have five senses: sight (eyes), hearing (ears), smell (nose), taste (tongue) and touch (skin).

question: how many teeth do adults have
how many teeth does an adult have
how many teeth do we have
answer: An adult has 32 teeth. Children have 20 baby teeth, which fall out and are replaced.

question: how do i keep my teeth healthy
why should i brush my teeth
how do i take care of my teeth
answer: Brush your teeth twice a day with a toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste, eat fewer sugary sweets, and visit the dentist. That prevents cavities!

question: what is a balanced diet
what are the food groups
what are the classes of food
what is healthy food
answer: A balanced diet has all the food classes: carbohydrates for energy (like yam, rice, cassava), proteins for growth (beans, fish, eggs), fats, vitamins and minerals (fruits and vegetables), fibre and water.

question: why should i wash my hands
how do i wash my hands
how do germs spread
what is hygiene
answer: Washing your hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds removes germs that can make you sick. Wash before eating, after using the toilet, and after playing outside.

question: what causes malaria
how do you get malaria
how can we prevent malaria
answer: Malaria is spread by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. To stay safe, sleep under a treated mosquito net, clear standing water where mosquitoes breed, and see a health worker quickly if you have a fever.

question: what is a vaccine
what are vaccines
why do we need vaccines
what is immunisation
answer: A vaccine teaches your body's defence system to recognise a germ safely, so it can fight the real germ later. Vaccines protect you and the people around you from serious diseases.

question: what is an atom
what are atoms
what is matter made of
answer: An atom is a tiny building block of everything. It has a nucleus in the middle, made of protons and neutrons, with electrons zooming around it. Atoms are far too small to see.

question: what is an element
what is the periodic table
how many elements are there
answer: An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom, like gold, oxygen and iron. The periodic table arranges all of the known elements, more than 100 of them.

question: what is the chemical symbol for water
what is water made of
what is h2o
answer: The chemical formula for water is H2O, which means each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

question: what is the chemical symbol for gold
what is the symbol for gold
what is the symbol for oxygen
what is the symbol for iron
answer: Chemical symbols: gold is Au, oxygen is O, iron is Fe, hydrogen is H, carbon is C and sodium is Na.

question: what is carbon dioxide
what gas do we breathe out
what gas do we need to breathe
what is oxygen
answer: We breathe in oxygen, which our bodies need. We breathe out carbon dioxide, which plants use to make food. Plants and animals help each other!

question: what is a mixture
what is a solution
what is dissolving
what is the difference between a mixture and a solution
answer: A mixture is made when two or more things are put together without changing them, like sand and gravel. A solution is made when something dissolves in a liquid, like sugar in water.

question: what is an acid
what is a base
what is ph
what is the ph scale
answer: Acids, like lemon juice and vinegar, taste sour and have a pH below 7. Bases, like soap, feel slippery and have a pH above 7. Pure water is neutral, at pH 7. Never taste science chemicals!

question: what is rusting
why does iron rust
how do i stop iron from rusting
answer: Rusting is when iron slowly turns reddish-brown and flaky because it reacts with oxygen and water. You can prevent it by painting, oiling or galvanising the iron.

question: what is a simple machine
what are simple machines
what is a lever
what is a pulley
what is an inclined plane
answer: Simple machines make work easier. The main ones are the lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane (a ramp), wedge and screw. A seesaw is a lever and a ramp is an inclined plane.

question: what is speed
how do i calculate speed
what is the formula for speed
answer: Speed is how fast something moves. Speed equals distance divided by time. If you walk 6 kilometres in 2 hours, your speed is 3 kilometres per hour.

question: what is weight
what is mass
what is the difference between mass and weight
answer: Mass is how much matter is in an object, measured in kilograms. Weight is how hard gravity pulls it down, so you'd weigh less on the Moon but your mass stays the same.

question: what is density
why do things float
why do things sink
what is floating and sinking
answer: Things float if they are less dense than the liquid, and they sink if they are more dense. A big wooden log floats, but a small stone sinks. Ships float because their shape holds a lot of air.

question: what is temperature
what is a thermometer
how do we measure temperature
answer: Temperature tells us how hot or cold something is. We measure it with a thermometer, in degrees Celsius. Body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius.

question: what is weather
what is climate
what is the difference between weather and climate
answer: Weather is what the sky and air are like today, like sunny, rainy or windy. Climate is the usual weather in a place over many years. Ghana has a warm tropical climate.

question: what is the harmattan
what is harmattan
when is the harmattan season
answer: The harmattan is a dry, dusty wind that blows from the Sahara Desert over West Africa, usually between late November and March. It makes mornings cool, the air hazy and the skin dry.

question: what is climate change
what is global warming
what is the greenhouse effect
answer: Climate change is the long-term warming of Earth, mainly because burning fossil fuels adds extra greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide that trap heat. We can help by saving energy, planting trees and wasting less.

question: what is recycling
why should we recycle
what is reduce reuse recycle
how can i help the environment
answer: Recycling turns old things, like plastic bottles, paper and metal cans, into new things. Remember the three Rs: reduce what you use, reuse what you can, and recycle the rest. Keeping Ghana clean helps everyone!

question: why is plastic bad for the environment
what is plastic pollution
why shouldn't i litter
answer: Plastic doesn't rot away. It stays for hundreds of years and can block drains and hurt animals in rivers and seas. Put rubbish in bins and pick up plastic when you can.

question: why are trees important
why should we plant trees
what do trees do for us
answer: Trees give us oxygen, shade, food, wood and homes for animals. Their roots hold the soil together, and they take in carbon dioxide, so planting trees helps fight climate change.

question: what is an earthquake
what is a volcano
what causes earthquakes
answer: An earthquake is shaking of the ground caused by huge pieces of Earth's crust moving. A volcano is an opening in the Earth where hot melted rock, called lava, comes out.

question: what are the layers of the earth
what is the earth made of
what is inside the earth
answer: The Earth has four layers: a thin outer crust that we live on, a thick mantle of hot rock, a liquid outer core, and a solid inner core of iron and nickel at the centre.

question: what are the types of rocks
how are rocks formed
what is an igneous rock
what is a sedimentary rock
what is a metamorphic rock
answer: There are three kinds of rocks. Igneous rocks form from cooled lava. Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sand and mud pressed together. Metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure.

question: what is soil
what types of soil are there
what is soil made of
answer: Soil is made of tiny pieces of rock, rotted plants and animals, air and water. The main kinds are sandy, clay and loamy soil, and loam is best for growing plants.

question: what is a fossil
what are fossils
how are fossils formed
answer: A fossil is the preserved remains or print of a plant or animal that lived long ago, usually found in rock.

question: what is a dinosaur
when did dinosaurs live
are dinosaurs alive today
what happened to the dinosaurs
answer: Dinosaurs were reptiles that lived on Earth for more than 150 million years. Most died out about 66 million years ago, probably after a huge asteroid hit the Earth. Birds are their living relatives!

question: what is the biggest animal
what is the largest animal in the world
what is the biggest animal on earth
answer: The blue whale is the biggest animal ever known. It can be about 25 to 30 metres long, nearly as long as three buses!

question: what is the fastest animal
what is the fastest land animal
which animal runs the fastest
answer: The cheetah is the fastest land animal. It can run at about 100 kilometres per hour for a short distance. The peregrine falcon is the fastest of all animals when it dives.

question: what is the tallest animal
which animal is the tallest
what is the tallest animal in the world
answer: The giraffe is the tallest animal. A grown giraffe can be about 5 metres tall!

question: what is the biggest land animal
which is the largest land animal
answer: The African elephant is the biggest land animal. It can weigh as much as 6,000 kilograms!

question: what is an endangered animal
what is extinction
why are animals going extinct
how can i protect animals
answer: An endangered animal is one that could soon disappear forever because there are very few left. Habitat loss, hunting and pollution are the main causes. We can protect animals by caring for forests, never buying wild animal products, and learning about nature.

question: what animals live in ghana
what wild animals are in ghana
what animals can i see at mole national park
tell me about wildlife in ghana
answer: Ghana has elephants, buffalo, antelopes, monkeys, crocodiles, hippos and many birds. Mole National Park is the biggest wildlife park, and you can see elephants there. Boabeng-Fiema is famous for its sacred monkeys!
